newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Italy's Telecom reports surge in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Italy's Telecom reports surge in 1996 profit.

text.p: Italian state-controlled phone company Telecom Italia, which is to be merged with its parent company Stet in preparation for sale to private investors, announced a big surge in 1996 profits on Friday.

Telecom said in a statement that net profit had jumped 53.7 percent to 2.119 trillion lire ($1.26 billion) as efforts by the company to slash costs, reduce debt and develop the business fed through to the bottom line.
The company said it would pay an increased dividend of 125 lire to holders of ordinary shares and of 145 lire to savings shareholders, compared with 120 lire and 140 lire respectively in 1995.

Later on Friday, the boards of Stet and Telecom Italia announced that the share swap ratio for Stet's merger with Telecom Italia was set at 1.8 ordinary Telecom shares for one ordinary Stet share, and 1.72 Telecom savings shares for every Stet savings share.

The boards announced in a statement that to carry out the operation Stet plans to increase its present capital of 5.281 trillion lire by a maximum of 2.170 trillion lire. The newly issued shares will have a nominal value of 1,000 lire each.
The statement said Stet's 1996 parent company net profit was 1.110 trillion lire, up from 1.104 trillion in 1995.

The Italian Treasury took control of Stet from state industrial holding IRI at the end of 1996 and intends to merge with Telecom Italia by June at the latest before the resulting company is privatised in the latter half of this year.
Stet, which is quoted in the United States as well as Milan, holds some 64 percent of Telecom Italia.

The statement by the two boards said that after the incorporation of Telecom into Stet, the Treasury's stake in Stet will fall to 44.7 percent of ordinary shares from a current 61.3 percent, and to 0.6 percent from 0.9 percent regarding the stake of savings shares.
Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said 10 to 15 percent of the capital of Stet should go to a stable group of shareholders with the rest put on the market to the public.
He said the government was seeking reliable partners for Stet, "ones without bias and therefore without conflict of interests."
Extraordinary shareholders' meetings of the two companies will be called to approve the merger plan on April 30.

Shares in Stet closed 2.0 percent up at 7,784 lire in Milan on Friday and Telecom Italia stock was 3.41 percent higher at 4,394 lire. Equity analysts said this was in line with expectations of a share swap ratio of 1.76 to 1.8. $=1,687
